//ApiBaseUrl: Primary API (MonsterASP). The scheme is cleartext http: because no certificate is bound to the runasp.net host (DEPLOYMENT.md 5 and 7).
//BackupApiBaseUrl: Empty on purpose. The Azure copy at https://verichat-api-aqcbgydhhbgbgha5.eastus-01.azurewebsites.net now reads its own database (VerichatDB, Entra-only) while this tier's primary reads the Monster database, so the two APIs hold different rows. Failing over between them would answer a read from the wrong dataset or write a ticket into the wrong system, which is worse than the request simply failing. ApiFallbackHandler disables itself when this key is empty. Restore it only when both APIs read one database and one Jwt:Key - DEPLOYMENT.md 7.3 and 7.7.
//Bootstrap: DemoUsers turns the one-click sign-in row on the login page (Views/Shared/_DemoQuickLogin.cshtml) and is the same key name the API's DemoUserSeeder reads, so one setting per host is the whole rule - see Services/DemoAccess.cs. Development is on implicitly, which is why appsettings.Development.json does not carry it; this file decides for a deployed run, and it says yes because the marker signs in from the published site. It is a rendering rule only: this tier never creates the accounts. Buttons on a host whose API did not seed them post real passwords at a user table that does not contain them and fail as a wrong password would. Anyone with the site address can open any role, including the administrator, because the seven passwords are in README.md - a deployment holding real data sets Bootstrap__DemoUsers=false here or in the host's app settings.
